interiors.headline: 97 people were on board.
interiors.body: 36 passengers and 61 crew, on the last leg of a transatlantic crossing from Frankfurt. Rain had passed. The airship circled, waiting for the wind to ease.

interiors.headline: It was filled with hydrogen.
interiors.body: Hydrogen gave the ship its lift. It also turned the hull into a fuel source, and the outer skin was treated with a flammable dope to keep the fabric tight.

interiors.headline: Then the rear fin flashed.
interiors.stat_label: Seconds from first flame to the ground
interiors.body: Witnesses saw the flash near the upper fin. The fire ran forward through the hull faster than anyone below could move.

interiors.headline: Thirty-six people died.
interiors.body: Thirty-five aboard and one on the ground. Sixty-two survived. The official cause is still undetermined: a hydrogen leak, ignited by static, with the spark never proven.

interiors.headline: It ended the airship era.
interiors.body: No commercial rigid airships were built after 1937. The mooring mast at Lakehurst is still standing.

cta.headline: Follow for the machines that changed history, and the failures that ended them.
